current_example.title: Example: Evaluating a Double Integral Over a Partitioned Region

q-132292.name: Question 1
q-132292.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2,$ and the lines $y=x+2,$ $x=-2$ and $x=2.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
q-132292.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/019f0f9f83ddf323d543d109677335cb3ae72a200baf834453a0eca16a9353ba.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/d222e86f6af7c3ed2b35711114c9062d6f0c9b0f2551aa44cac33318c6e5813f.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le 0,\,x+2\le y\le \frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}+2\le y\le x+2\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{x+2}^{{x}^{2}/2+2}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}/2+2}^{x+2}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 1
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve y=x22+2, and the lines y=x+2, x=−2 and x=2. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫−20∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx
b
∫−20∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx
c
∫−20∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx
d
∫−21∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫12∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−20∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−2≤x≤0,x+2≤y≤x22+2}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤x≤2,x22+2≤y≤x+2}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−20∫x+2x2/2+2f(x,y)dydx+∫02∫x2/2+2x+2f(x,y)dydx.

q-132296.name: Question 2
q-132296.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=\frac{3x}{2}+6,$ $y=-3x-3$ and $y=0.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
q-132296.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/8dad5cdaa9fdcaf0293773c53a0b5ab58d7d98aea0099af0a9ba616e72759129.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/a0b5bfe05214df5f59a563677bd6b4f7dfd85be4d8e27fd4d7b31f87a679cd2b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-4\le x\le -2,\,0\le y\le \frac{3x}{2}+6\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le x\le -1,\,0\le y\le -3x-3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-4}^{-2}{\int }_{0}^{3x/2+6}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx+{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{\int }_{0}^{-3x-3}f(x,y)\,dy\,dx.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 2
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=3x2+6, y=−3x−3 and y=0. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫−4−2∫3x/2+60f(x,y)dydx+∫−2−1∫0−3x−3f(x,y)dydx
b
 ∫−2−1∫03x/2+6f(x,y)dydx+∫−10∫0−3x−3f(x,y)dydx
c
∫−4−2∫03x/2+6f(x,y)dydx+∫−2−1∫−3x−30f(x,y)dydx
d
∫−2−1∫03x/2+6f(x,y)dydx+∫−10∫−3x−30f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−4−2∫03x/2+6f(x,y)dydx+∫−2−1∫0−3x−3f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−4≤x≤−2,0≤y≤3x2+6}

and

D2={(x,y):−2≤x≤−1,0≤y≤−3x−3}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−4−2∫03x/2+6f(x,y)dydx+∫−2−1∫0−3x−3f(x,y)dydx.

q-37758.name: Question 3
q-37758.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/7e979ac75636efa00cbc32ee92eff1a5fc1da3cea19378fbf5a39a5cc954ff45.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y={x}^{2}$ and lines $y=7x,$ $y=x+12,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
q-37758.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/ee6fd6a0b89a879d5803a98fda7e80a93926566995bea5f47a05aa7ab2986375.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 2,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le 7x\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x+12\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{7x}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x+12}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-37758.html:
Question 3
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve y=x2 and lines y=7x, y=x+12, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫02∫x+127xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫0x2f(x,y)dydx
b
∫02∫x27xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫x27xf(x,y)dydx
c
∫02∫x2x+12f(x,y)dydx+∫24∫x2x+12f(x,y)dydx
d
∫02∫x27xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫x2x+12f(x,y)dydx
e
∫02∫x2x+12f(x,y)dydx+∫24∫7xx2f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤x≤2,x2≤y≤7x}

and

D2={(x,y):2≤x≤4,x2≤y≤x+12}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫02∫x27xf(x,y)dydx+∫24∫x2x+12f(x,y)dydx.
q-37758.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type I Regions

q-82075.name: Question 4
q-82075.problem:
Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $x=3-{y}^{2}$ and the line $y=1-x.$ 
Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
q-82075.worked_solution:
First, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/8a46756cd4842caf7977ef72ae05912a635843a06382b21136362455a94369e4.png)

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.   Notice that we're using that $x=3-{y}^{2}$ can be split into $y=\pm \sqrt{3-x}.$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/43da7a61d7a4bff15274cdacbf1f3265c097edb8740583c69463460467f8100f.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 2,\,1-x\le y\le \sqrt{3-x}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 3,\,-\sqrt{3-x}\le y\le \sqrt{3-x}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{2}{\int }_{1-x}^{\sqrt{3-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{-\sqrt{3-x}}^{\sqrt{3-x}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-82075.html:
Question 4
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve x=3−y2 and the line y=1−x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫−12∫1−x3−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫23∫03−xf(x,y)dydx
b
∫−12∫1−x3−y2f(x,y)dydx+∫23∫03−y2f(x,y)dydx
c
∫−12∫1−x3−x2f(x,y)dydx+∫−13∫−3−x3−xf(x,y)dydx
d
∫−12∫1−x3−xf(x,y)dydx+∫23∫−3−x3−xf(x,y)dydx
e
∫−13∫1−x3−xf(x,y)dydx+∫23∫x−33−xf(x,y)dydx
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below. Notice that we're using that x=3−y2 can be split into y=±3−x.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):−1≤x≤2,1−x≤y≤3−x}

and

D2={(x,y):2≤x≤3,−3−x≤y≤3−x}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−12∫1−x3−xf(x,y)dydx+∫23∫−3−x3−xf(x,y)dydx.

q-132290.name: Question 5
q-132290.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/797cddb4ea3cb41959df88e56517e9ee71e76e3cd08a9a93d2957b9792d14abb.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-\frac{2x}{3},$ $y=\frac{4x}{3}$ and $y=\frac{x}{3}+3,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.
q-132290.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/0e69b1cb480b87216273db4336adff57cbf9d9bc450aac4b0cdb58b1ae63f6f7.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-3\le x\le 0,\,-\frac{2x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\frac{4x}{3}\le y\le \frac{x}{3}+3\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-3}^{0}{\int }_{-2x/3}^{x/3+3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{3}{\int }_{4x/3}^{x/3+3}f(x,y)\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

q-132290.html:
Question 5
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=−2x3, y=4x3 and y=x3+3, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type I regions.

a
∫−30∫x/3+3−2x/3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫4x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx
b
∫−30∫4x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫−2x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx
c
∫−30∫−2x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫x/3+34x/3f(x,y)dydx
d
∫−30∫x/3+3−2x/3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫x/3+34x/3f(x,y)dydx
e
∫−30∫−2x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫4x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−3≤x≤0,−2x3≤y≤x3+3}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤x≤3,4x3≤y≤x3+3}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−30∫−2x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx+∫03∫4x/3x/3+3f(x,y)dydx.
q-132290.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type I Regions

q-132397.name: Question 6
q-132397.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=6-4x$ and $y=2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
q-132397.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-x & \,⟹\,x=-y \\ y=6-4x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4} \\ y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/08237d1ca2e01d0cf620dfa06a4265d8053b7ee34d0b65036aad7d5734726e1c.png)

 

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/c756dc7924fc4c116601da907eb3b767b8a40647e063c146dad83b0ea660933b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-2\le y\le 0,\,-y\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \frac{3}{2}-\frac{y}{4}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-2}^{0}{\int }_{-y}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y/2}^{3/2-y/4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 6

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=−x, y=6−4x and y=2x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫−20∫−y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫2y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy
b
∫−20∫3/2−y/4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫−20∫6−4y−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫2y6−4yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫3/2−y/4y/2f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows: y=−x⟹x=−yy=6−4x⟹x=32−y4y=2x⟹x=y2

Now, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):−2≤y≤0,−y≤x≤32−y4} and D2={(x,y):0≤y≤2,y2≤x≤32−y4}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫−20∫−y3/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫y/23/2−y/4f(x,y)dxdy.

q-82358.name: Question 7
q-82358.problem: Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curve $y=\sqrt{x-2}+1,$ and the lines $y=2-\frac{1}{2}x$ and $y=8-2x.$ Express ${∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
q-82358.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\sqrt{x-2}+1 & \,⟹\,x=(y-1)^{2}+2 \\ y=2-\frac{1}{2}x & \,⟹\,x=4-2y \\ y=8-2x & \,⟹\,x=4-\frac{1}{2}y\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's sketch our region.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/3f8e3ccfeac236d7fe9a502f599c61c404607a55ae809ec142019a3f881e1568.png)

  

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/3148cb0f499564db9cbfd6b635fef81dc47298789241af4a243c32dbf4dc8247.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,4-2y\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,(y-1)^{2}+2\le x\le 4-\frac{1}{2}y\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{4-2y}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(y-1)^{2}+2}^{4-y/2}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

q-82358.html:
Question 7
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curve y=x−2+1, and the lines y=2−12x and y=8−2x. Express ∬Df(x,y)dA as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−2yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫01∫04−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows:

y=x−2+1⟹x=(y−1)2+2y=2−12x⟹x=4−2yy=8−2x⟹x=4−12y

Now, let's sketch our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,4−2y≤x≤4−12y}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤2,(y−1)2+2≤x≤4−12y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫4−2y4−y/2f(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(y−1)2+24−y/2f(x,y)dxdy.

q-132380.name: Question 8
q-132380.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/4826bc628c1bd8f4293fd5fbf90bf9155658c15336c2c9e86a5e7678dfcf1ca3.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=-x,$ $y=x+4,$ $y=0$ and $y=4,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
q-132380.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=-x & \,⟹\,x=-y \\ y=x+4 & \,⟹\,x=y-4\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/17d3ceabf3cd7a052398d8d12b7963c5ca64356605554e3ff43c21c7321e45de.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 2,\,y-4\le x\le -y\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le y\le 4,\,-y\le x\le y-4\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-4}^{-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{-y}^{y-4}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

q-132380.html:
Question 8
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=−x, y=x+4, y=0 and y=4, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫02∫y+4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫−yy+4f(x,y)dxdy
b
∫02∫y−4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫−yy−4f(x,y)dxdy
c
∫02∫y+4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫y+4−yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫02∫−yy−4f(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫−yy−4f(x,y)dxdy
e
∫02∫y−4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫y−4−yf(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows: y=−x⟹x=−yy=x+4⟹x=y−4

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get D1={(x,y):0≤y≤2,y−4≤x≤−y}

and

D2={(x,y):2≤y≤4,−y≤x≤y−4}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain ∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫02∫y−4−yf(x,y)dxdy+∫24∫−yy−4f(x,y)dxdy.
q-132380.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type II Regions

q-82116.name: Question 9
q-82116.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/7fa5e4cd0c573ab5841e3ded221486ee2cabf6e00e1493c3de06fe4d9a87e3a7.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the lines $y=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2},$ $y=2x,$ and $y=\frac{(2x+2)}{3},$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
q-82116.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y=\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2} & \,⟹\,x=\sqrt{2y} \\ y=2x & \,⟹\,x=\frac{y}{2} \\ y=\frac{2x+2}{3} & \,⟹\,x=\frac{3y-2}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/63848a26cff0641ac83c73e809028852697212ce64a8cb954815d514922721a1.png)

  

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,\frac{y}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2y}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 2,\,\frac{3y-2}{2}\le x\le \sqrt{2y}\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{y/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{(3y-2)/2}^{\sqrt{2y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the lines y=12x2, y=2x, and y=(2x+2)3, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
 ∫01∫y2yf(x,y)dydx+∫12∫(3y−2)/22yf(x,y)dydx
b
 ∫02∫y/22yf(x,y)dxdy+∫01∫(3y+2)/22yf(x,y)dxdy
c
 ∫01∫y2/22yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(2y+2)/32yf(x,y)dxdy
d
 ∫01∫y/22yf(x,y)dxdy+∫02∫(3y+2)/22yf(x,y)dxdy
e
 ∫01∫y/22yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(3y−2)/22yf(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows:

y=12x2⟹x=2yy=2x⟹x=y2y=2x+23⟹x=3y−22

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,y2≤x≤2y}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤2,3y−22≤x≤2y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫y/22yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12∫(3y−2)/22yf(x,y)dxdy.

q-82135.name: Question 10
q-82135.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/4174f3930bb19223300539e1b4e9b7b191669aa4f701bff51e8349d0710ce6fb.png)

Consider the finite region $D$ in the $xy$-plane enclosed by the curves $y={e}^{x},$ $y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x,$ and the lines $y=1+e-x$  and $y=1-x,$ as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function $f(x,y)$ over the region $D$ as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.
q-82135.worked_solution:
First, let's write our equations in terms of $y,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}y={e}^{x} & \,⟹\,x=\operatorname{ln}⁡y \\ y=\operatorname{ln}⁡x & \,⟹\,x={e}^{y} \\ y=1+e-x & \,⟹\,x=1+e-y \\ y=1-x & \,⟹\,x=1-y\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type II regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/4df7cf2f33520a80270341d4a40b4a83d9f3c11ed8adb69fe1131a42bcd61d5a.png)

    

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1-y\le x\le {e}^{y}\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le e,\,\operatorname{ln}⁡y\le x\le 1+e-y\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}f(x,y)\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}f(x,y)\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1-y}^{{e}^{y}}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{e}{\int }_{\operatorname{ln}⁡y}^{1+e-y}f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}

q-82135.html:
Question 10
?

Consider the finite region D in the xy-plane enclosed by the curves y=ex, y=ln⁡x, and the lines y=1+e−x and y=1−x, as shown in the picture. Express the double integral of the function f(x,y) over the region D as a sum of repeated integrals over type II regions.

a
∫01∫1−yln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
b
∫02∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫2e∫ln⁡ye−yf(x,y)dxdy
c
∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
d
∫01∫−ye2yf(x,y)dxdy+∫12e∫−ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy
e
∫01/2∫1−y+eln⁡yf(x,y)dxdy+∫1/2e∫ln⁡y1−yf(x,y)dxdy
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

First, let's write our equations in terms of y, as follows:

y=ex⟹x=ln⁡yy=ln⁡x⟹x=eyy=1+e−x⟹x=1+e−yy=1−x⟹x=1−y

The region D can be partitioned into two type II regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):0≤y≤1,1−y≤x≤ey}

and

D2={(x,y):1≤y≤e,ln⁡y≤x≤1+e−y}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬Df(x,y)dA=∬D1f(x,y)dA+∬D2f(x,y)dA=∫01∫1−yeyf(x,y)dxdy+∫1e∫ln⁡y1+e−yf(x,y)dxdy.
q-82135.knowledge_point: Representing a Double Integral as a Repeated Integral Over a Union of Type II Regions

q-132423.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/a4265e8993b5c7ea5756fe55facd5313e5c2237cbdbc851195ebf458e5246060.png)

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}2y\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
q-132423.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/33a38da74b282f0ec1fb2fae9cb155feb2a5fd39128c7607b80c6b84fedd29b4.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le x\le 2,\,x-1\le y\le 3-x\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,2\le x\le 4,\,3-x\le y\le x-1\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{\int }_{x-1}^{3-x}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{\int }_{3-x}^{x-1}2y\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{x-1}^{3-x}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}{y}^{2}\,{|}_{3-x}^{x-1}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}[(3-x)^{2}-(x-1)^{2}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}[(x-1)^{2}-(3-x)^{2}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{2}(8-4x)\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{4}(4x-8)\text{d}x \\  & =(8x-2{x}^{2}){|}_{1}^{2}+(2{x}^{2}-8x){|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =8(2-1)-2({2}^{2}-{1}^{2})+2({4}^{2}-{2}^{2})-8(4-2) \\  & =8-6+24-16 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4xy\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}4xy\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}4xy\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{1}^{3}4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{\int }_{0}^{3}4xy\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{[2x{y}^{2}]}_{1}^{3}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}{[2x{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{3}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}2x(9-1)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}2x(9-0)\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}16x\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{3}18x\,\text{d}x \\  & =8{x}^{2}{|}_{0}^{2}+9{x}^{2}{|}_{2}^{3} \\  & =8(4-0)+9(9-4) \\  & =77.\end{aligned}
$$

The region $D$ is enclosed by the the curves $y={x}^{2}$ and $y=|x|,$ as shown in the picture. Evaluate ${∬}_{D}2x\,dA.$
q-82360.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into two type I regions ${D}_{1}$ and ${D}_{2},$ as shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/2fcb30778db2f051a7a819ae701808af59ac18d27c25a9c57ce678caa6c3ee3b.png)

As a result, we get

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,-1\le x\le 0,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le -x\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 1,\,{x}^{2}\le y\le x\}.
$$

 

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}2x\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}2x\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}2x\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{-x}2x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{{x}^{2}}^{x}2x\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}2xy{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{-x}\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}2xy{|}_{{x}^{2}}^{x}\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}2x[-x-{x}^{2}]\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}2x[x-{x}^{2}]\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}(-2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}(2{x}^{2}-2{x}^{3})\text{d}x \\  & ={[-\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{-1}^{0}+{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}-\frac{1}{2}{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =((0-(-\frac{2}{3}(-1)^{3}-\frac{1}{2}(-1)^{4}))+((\frac{2}{3}(1)^{3}-\frac{1}{2}(1)^{4})-0)) \\  & =-\frac{1}{6}+\frac{1}{6} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{|x|+|y|\le 1}{e}^{x+y}\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}{e}^{x+y}\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}{e}^{x+y}\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}{\int }_{-x-1}^{x+1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{x-1}^{-x+1}{e}^{x+y}\,\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}[{e}^{x+y}]_{-x-1}^{x+1}\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}[{e}^{x+y}]_{x-1}^{-x+1}\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{-1}^{0}({e}^{2x+1}-{e}^{-1})\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{1}(e-{e}^{2x-1})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={[\frac{{e}^{2x+1}}{2}-{e}^{-1}x]}_{-1}^{0}+{[ex-\frac{{e}^{2x-1}}{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =[\frac{e}{2}-(\frac{{e}^{-1}}{2}+{e}^{-1})]+[(e-\frac{e}{2})+\frac{{e}^{-1}}{2}] \\  & =e-{e}^{-1}.\end{aligned}
$$

∬|x|+|y|≤1ex+ydA=

a
 e−e−12
b
 2(e−e−1)
c

e
 e−e−12
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, let's draw a sketch of our region.

The region D can be partitioned into two type I regions D1 and D2, as shown below.

As a result, we get

D1={(x,y):−1≤x≤0,−x−1≤y≤x+1}

and

D2={(x,y):0≤x≤1,x−1≤y≤−x+1}.

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain

∬|x|+|y|≤1ex+ydA=∬D1ex+ydA+∬D2ex+ydA=∫−10∫−x−1x+1ex+ydydx+∫01∫x−1−x+1ex+ydydx=∫−10[ex+y]−x−1x+1dx+∫01[ex+y]x−1−x+1dx=∫−10(e2x+1−e−1)dx+∫01(e−e2x−1)dx=[e2x+12−e−1x]−10+[ex−e2x−12]01=[e2−(e−12+e−1)]+[(e−e2)+e−12]=e−e−1.

Evaluate ${∬}_{D}{x}^{2}y\,dA,$ where $D$ is the region shown in the picture above.
q-37767.worked_solution:
The region $D$ can be partitioned into three type II regions ${D}_{1},$ ${D}_{2},$ and ${D}_{3},$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14153479/assets/b58fc3909d5be467999053336f67d41b88b43c984208c60f3d46ee8b7479df58.png)

As a result, we get 

$$
{D}_{1}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,-2\le x\le -1\},
$$

$$
{D}_{2}=\{(x,y)\,:\,0\le y\le 1,\,1\le x\le 2\}
$$

and 

$$
{D}_{3}=\{(x,y)\,:\,1\le y\le 3,\,-2\le x\le 2\}.
$$

Therefore, using the additivity property of double integrals, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}{x}^{2}y\,dA & ={∬}_{{D}_{1}}{x}^{2}y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{2}}{x}^{2}y\,dA+{∬}_{{D}_{3}}{x}^{2}y\,dA \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-2}^{-1}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{1}^{2}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}{\int }_{-2}^{2}{x}^{2}y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{-1}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{1}^{2}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}{[\frac{y\text{ }\,{x}^{3}}{3}]}_{-2}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7y}{3}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7y}{3}\,\text{d}y+{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{16y}{3}\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\cdot \frac{7}{3}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{1}+\frac{16}{3}\cdot {[\frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{7}{3}+\frac{64}{3} \\  & =\frac{71}{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
